reviewer: Claude (Opus 5, Claude Code) -- all 58 sheets opened and read tile by tile, 2026-08-22
period_and_place: Atlanta suburb 2017 and the paper years to 2026. Interiors, offices and filing rooms are deliberately period-neutral; the Collinsville 1973-74 act carries 1970s cars and typewriters and is signalled by its own date cards, so no anachronism asserts a wrong decade.
method: Every sheet read at full size, 1158 frames over 287 cuts. Ship-policy question only; craft observations are notes.

prohibition_checks.real_person_likeness: NONE. Martin, Cliatt, G.W., Guerra and every agent are avoided entirely -- the film shows hands, boots, backs and silhouettes and never a resolved face. The raid team appears only as unlit silhouettes from behind (34:45-34:51). The AI-assisted visualization card runs at 0:05 and again at 39:29. The seven-year-old is a shape under a blanket, never a child's face.
prohibition_checks.rights_and_licence: No watermark, logo, generator mark or readable brand on any tile. Vehicles carry no badges; the mailbox and street signs carry no legible address.
prohibition_checks.factual_support: Every quote card names its source in the rule below it -- MARTIN v. UNITED STATES (2025) opinion of the Court, Sotomayor J. concurring quoting the Senate committee, and the 29 April 2025 oral argument transcript with the speaker named (Gorsuch, Sotomayor, Mr Liu). The two arithmetic cards (44 years, 8 years) say 'our arithmetic' on the card itself.
prohibition_checks.fabricated_record: No legible generated document anywhere. Warrants, dockets, opinions, file folders and correspondence are blank stock, texture or defocused; every readable passage on screen is typography-on-black with its citation.

notes: 287 cuts, zero factory/stock footage in the film -- the picture is entirely this episode's own plates and their i2v motion. Endcard brand card 39:51-39:58 and a clean last frame. Craft notes only: the film is dark by design (night suburb, unlit interiors) and leans on desk/file/corridor motifs in the middle acts; both are consistent, neither is a policy question.
